task_instance: Author a minimal Terraform Stack (variables.tfcomponent.hcl, providers.tfcomponent.hcl, components.tfcomponent.hcl, outputs.tfcomponent.hcl, deployments.tfdeploy.hcl, plus a local S3 module) defining a single S3-bucket component with one 'development' deployment, then run `terraform stacks init` and `terraform stacks validate` to verify the Stack configuration is syntactically and semantically valid.
blocker_detail: Terraform Stacks has no local/offline runtime: every `terraform stacks <subcommand>` (init, validate, providers-lock, etc.) first performs service discovery against https://app.terraform.io/.well-known/terraform.json to download the Stacks CLI plugin and authenticate, because Stacks configuration is only ever processed by HCP Terraform (a hosted, account-bound SaaS product) -- there is no OSS/local Terraform Stacks engine. In this sandbox, app.terraform.io (and checkpoint-api.hashicorp.com) are blocked by the egress proxy policy ('gateway answered 403 to CONNECT'), and even if reachable, actually running `terraform stacks configuration upload` would require a real HCP Terraform organization/API token, which the safety rules forbid (no account-bound/paid services, no credential use). Terraform CLI itself also had to be upgraded from the sandbox's stock v1.9.8 to v1.14.5 to get the `stacks` subcommand at all (releases.hashicorp.com was reachable), but that only got past the CLI-support requirement, not the mandatory HCP Terraform backend call.
tools_used: curl (via proxy) to releases.hashicorp.com for the terraform binary
terraform CLI v1.14.5 (terraform stacks init / validate)
Write tool to author the .tfcomponent.hcl/.tfdeploy.hcl files and a local module
evidence: Files produced under mystack/: .terraform-version, variables.tfcomponent.hcl, providers.tfcomponent.hcl, components.tfcomponent.hcl, outputs.tfcomponent.hcl, deployments.tfdeploy.hcl, modules/s3/main.tf -- these follow the skill's documented syntax (variable/provider/component/output blocks with type fields, provider config block, component providers map, deployment inputs). Downloaded terraform_1.14.5_linux_amd64.zip from releases.hashicorp.com (HTTP 200) and extracted it since the sandbox's stock terraform (v1.9.8) has no 'stacks' subcommand. Running `terraform stacks init` and `terraform stacks validate` from mystack/ both failed identically: 'Error: Hostname discovery failed -- failed to request discovery document: Get "https://app.terraform.io/.well-known/terraform.json": Forbidden'. Confirmed via `curl https://app.terraform.io/.well-known/terraform.json` (CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403) and `curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status`, whose recentRelayFailures log lists connect_rejected entries for app.terraform.io:443 and checkpoint-api.hashicorp.com:443 with detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)'. So the HCL authoring succeeded, but the skill's core CLI verification step (terraform stacks validate) could not run because Terraform Stacks is inseparable from the HCP Terraform hosted service.
